content.user_title: Convert Notion Specs Into Implementation Tasks
content.value_statement: Teams often lose detail when moving from Notion specs to engineering work. This skill turns a spec into linked plans, tasks, and progress updates inside Notion.
actual_capabilities: Finds and fetches a Notion spec through Notion MCP tools.
Extracts requirements, acceptance criteria, constraints, priorities, and gaps.
Creates quick or standard implementation plans linked to the source spec.
Builds task pages with objectives, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and provided owners.
Updates spec, plan, and task pages with progress, blockers, and decisions.
limitations: Requires an authenticated Notion MCP connection before it can access workspace pages.
Does not implement application code; it organizes implementation work.
Depends on available Notion database schemas and user-granted permissions.
May need user clarification when specs are ambiguous or search results match multiple pages.

use_cases.title: Turn PRDs Into Execution Plans
use_cases.description: Create a structured implementation plan from a Notion PRD, including risks, phases, and success criteria.

use_cases.title: Break Specs Into Engineering Tasks
use_cases.description: Convert a feature spec into scoped task pages with objectives, acceptance criteria, and dependencies.

use_cases.title: Maintain Delivery Status
use_cases.description: Keep linked plans and tasks current with progress updates, blockers, decisions, and milestone summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Plan From a Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Notion spec titled "[spec name]" to create a quick implementation plan and list any open questions first.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Linked Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the implementation plan for "[feature name]", confirm the task database schema, then create 1-2 day tasks linked to the spec and plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Phase Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the Notion spec for "[migration name]" and build a standard implementation plan with phases, dependencies, risks, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Run Progress Management
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the linked plan and tasks for "[project name]", update statuses, summarize blockers, and add a milestone summary for completed work.

output_examples.input: A Notion spec for a dashboard filter feature needs execution planning.
output: A linked implementation plan with scope, requirements, open questions, phases, and success criteria.
Task pages for design review, API changes, UI work, testing, and release notes.

output_examples.input: A database migration spec has several dependencies and rollout risks.
output: A standard plan with migration phases, dependency notes, rollback criteria, and validation checkpoints.
Tasks sized for analysis, schema updates, backfill work, monitoring, and final cleanup.

output_examples.input: A team wants weekly progress tracking for a feature already planned in Notion.
output: Updated task statuses, a concise blocker summary, and a milestone note linked to the active plan.
A clear list of decisions, completed work, and next actions for the next update cycle.

best_practices: Confirm the correct Notion page when search returns multiple specs.
Resolve missing requirements before creating tasks that assume product behavior.
Use small tasks with clear acceptance criteria and linked source pages.
anti_patterns: Creating tasks from an outdated spec without checking recent changes.
Skipping database schema checks before writing Notion task pages.
Using this skill in a workspace where you lack permission to update pages.

faq.question: What does this skill need to work?
faq.answer: It needs an authenticated Notion MCP connection with access to the relevant spec, plan, and task pages.

faq.question: Can it write to Notion?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create and update Notion pages when the connected account has permission.

faq.question: Does it generate application code?
faq.answer: No. It creates implementation plans, task pages, and progress updates from Notion specs.

faq.question: How does it handle unclear specs?
faq.answer: It captures gaps and assumptions, then asks for clarification before creating dependent work items.

faq.question: Can it manage ongoing progress?
faq.answer: Yes. It can update statuses, summarize blockers, and add milestone summaries to linked Notion pages.

faq.question: Is it useful for small changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use a quick implementation plan for focused changes that do not need a full project plan.
